jobs.title: Labour Relations Officer
jobs.excerpt: The National Police Federation is currently hiring a Labour Relations Officer to join our team.
jobs.description:
The National Police Federation is currently hiring a Labour Relations Officer to join our team.

Overview of the Role: The Labour Relations Officer (LRO) plays a key role in fostering positive and productive relationships between Members and their employer within a unionized environment. This position involves interpreting and applying labour laws, negotiating and administering collective agreements, mediating disputes, and advising on policies and procedures. The LRO also provides technical advice, representation, and procedural guidance to Members, Local Area Representatives (LARs), and Regional Directors on complex or specialized labour relations matters.

Reporting to: Labour Relations Officer Supervisor

Location: Canada-wide (Remote)

Who We Are:

The National Police Federation (NPF) represents ~20,000 RCMP Members serving across Canada and internationally. We are the largest police union in Canada. The NPF is focused on improving public safety for all Canadians, including our Members by advocating for much-needed investment in the public safety continuum. This includes investments in police resourcing and modern equipment, as well as social programs including health, addiction, and housing supports to enhance safety and livability in the many communities we serve, large and small, across Canada.

Our head office is located in Ottawa but our 70+ staff work remotely across Canada. We stay closely connected through our up-to-date I.T. tools and by living our internal values: Inclusion, Innovation, Appreciation, Collaboration, and Trust.

Why Work with the NPF?

  • Competitive compensation package.
  • Generous Group Benefit package including Health Care Spending and Taxable Spending Accounts.
  • Competitive pension matching program of up to 7%.
  • Professional development opportunities.
  • An inclusive, passionate, and fun team environment.

Key Responsibilities:

Support and guidance

  • Independently read, analyze, and interpret various resources, such as the collective agreement, the RCMP (Royal Canadian Mounted Police) Act, and RCMP policies and procedures to provide timely advice to NPF (National Police Federation) Members regarding fact specific, individual circumstances.
  • Identify any issues that may require further analysis or interpretation, particularly those involving the Membership as a whole, and those situations which fall under statutes.
  • Refer issues to other NPF employees such as Legal Counsel, LR Team Lead or NPF Directors for further clarification. 
  • Subject to availability, is ready to immediately deploy, and/or respond/support to critical incidents involving NPF Members.
  • Provide support to Members involved in critical incidents, including through providing information on their rights and responsibilities during investigations by external bodies and the RCMP (ASIRT (Alberta Serious Incident Response Team), IIO (Independent Investigations Office), Coroner, MCU etc.).
  • Ensure Members have immediate access to available support, including medical and mental health.
  • Liaise with the Employer to ensure NPF Members are being supported and are being provided with information.
  • Gather information and provide updates as required to NPF Staff, NPF Directors, and Local Area Representatives.
  • If required, act as a point of contact for RCMP management, RCMP supervisors, and NPF Members. 

Representation to NPF Members

  • Write legally sound and/or policy driven submissions on behalf of the NPF and/or Member for grievances and Codes of Conduct and present them during hearings and/or meetings.
  • Mentor Local Area Representatives to support meetings when the LRO is unable to attend in-person.
  • Engage with Employer counterparts such as HSOs (Health Services Officer), CDROs (Career Development Resourcing Officer), CDRAs (Career Development and Resourcing Advisor), CMLRAs (Corporate Member Labour Relations Advisor), EMROs (Employee & Management Relations Office) etc. to proactively problem-solve/negotiate resolutions to Member labour issues through informal discussions.
  • Consult with others such as legal counsel, external counsel (PAF), other NPF Staff and NPF Board Directors when required.
  • Follow the guidance and instructions of the NPF LR Team Lead, LR Program Manager as directed.
  • Research and knowledge sharing
  • Independently conduct research, access legal resources and RCMP policies, and stay current on jurisprudence and developments related to labour relations/labour law and apply the relevance to Member issues.
  • Participate in ongoing labour relations education through coursework, conferences, and online learning to meet the NPF’s goal of providing accurate advice. 
  • Professional Develpment with yearly courses and training to remain current with updated Labour Laws and case law. Attend meetings with NPF Directors and Employer representatives (such as the National Policy Health and Safety Committee) to observe, collaborate, and provide technical guidance.
  • Participate in regular team meetings to share information with other Labour Relations Officers.
  • Support training for Local Area Representatives and new Labour Relations Officers to share institutional knowledge and subject matter expertise.
  • Engage and liaise to collaboratively identify issues and elevate concerns and trends that affect the general NPF Membership. 

Special projects

  • Take lead on major files involving multiple Members and/or are expected to result in multiple intakes (Wildfires, Floods, IVF, Mat/Pat, IMEs etc.).
  • Liaise as required with assigned Director on major events (COP15, Papal Visits, G7, and G20 etc.).
  • Consult with NPF Legal to develop policy grievances for matters affecting the entire bargaining unit.
  • Provide updates on the progress of these files to NPF Directors, NPF management, and NPF Members. 

DFR/ Representation Policy

  • Understand and utilize information contained within the NPF Representation Policy to respond to inquiries from NPF Members.
  • Inform Members of their rights contained within the Policy and provide input to NPF leadership and NPF Legal regarding a Member’s complaint.
  • Maintain knowledge of the duty of fair representation and apply this knowledge during their day-to-day work.
  • Liaise with NPF Legal on any matters involving the duty of fair representation.
  • Assist the NPF in gathering information about a complaint and by gathering documentation needed to assist with assessing the merits of the Member’s concerns. 

Record management

  • Ensure records are up-to date by updating NPF systems (such as Galexy, etc.).
  • Record in detail interactions with Members and Employer representatives in NPF systems to ensure an accurate and timely record of correspondence is retained.

Qualifications/Key Attributes:

  • A degree in labour relations or a related field and/or a combination of education and experience in the field of labour relations/law enforcement/human resources.
  • Experience in a labour relations program, association and/or unionized representation, primarily in one or more of these areas: Career Development/Staffing, Transfer/Relocation, Workplace Conflict, Disability Management, Accommodation, Grievances, Conduct, Serious Incidents, and Harassment. With preference to having experience in multiple areas.
  • Significant and recent experience in representing employees experiencing workplace issues.
  • A graduate degree in labour relations or a related field may be seen as an asset.
  • Experience working in a law enforcement environment an asset.
  • Experience with case management / file management systems is an asset.
  • Advanced working knowledge of labour relations principles, collective agreements, and/or a variety of workplace policies and procedures
  • Strong understanding of occupational health and safety, workplace accommodation, and disability management is an asset.
  • Effective and persuasive communication skills, orally and written. Ability to communicate complex topics to colleagues, Local representatives, and Employer representatives. Providing advice and guidance to NPF Members.
  • Must be highly proficient with Microsoft Office Productivity tools (Teams and Outlook).
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills, including the ability to build professional relationships across all aspects and levels of the NPF.
  • Ability to exercise leadership and diplomacy amongst diverse perspectives and priorities.
  • Ability to adapt to changing situations, current ideas, and concepts.
  • High level of attention to detail.
  • Excellent problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to multi-task; take the initiative; be proactive; flexible.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet continuous deadlines.

Other Requirements

Travel required 5-10/year. 

Must successfully pass a pre-employment criminal record check.

Compensation & Other Important Information:

The starting base salary for this position is $114,775.86. The ability to advance through the salary range for this position will be based on performance through our annual performance review program.

Starting annual leave for this position is four weeks (accrued as earned) which increases to five weeks after five years of employment with the NPF.

There is room for growth with supervisor and management positions within the Labour Relations team.

Further, while requiring some travel in your province and across Canada is a requirement for this role, our remote work model includes flexibility in completing work hours and a philosophy in promoting a positive work-life balance.

While we welcome applications from all interested individuals, only those candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

IT Help Desk Specialist

  • Location: Remote. International applicants welcome.

About the role

We run sales and support teams across several health and wellness brands. Everything they do runs on Salesforce, a cloud phone system and a business texting platform. When something breaks, you're the one who fixes it.

You'll be the first point of contact for 150+ users: their accounts, their phone setup and their support tickets. You'll escalate only what truly needs a system change.

How we work

This role is built for someone who doesn't need to be managed. There's no daily task list handed to you. Your work lives on a dashboard that shows every open ticket, pending request and system alert, and your goal is to keep it empty.

We're looking for someone who:

  • Starts the day by checking the dashboard, not by waiting for direction

  • Figures things out before asking

  • Manages their own time and priorities, and knows what's urgent and what can wait until the afternoon

  • Follows through without reminders and closes the loop with the person who asked

  • Can be trusted with admin access to the tools the whole company depends on

If you do your best work with clear ownership and little supervision, this is that job.

  • Keep the help desk dashboard at zero: open tickets, pending account requests and system health alerts

  • Resolve most support tickets yourself, and escalate the rest with the investigation already done

  • Set up and remove user accounts across Salesforce, Vonage, SMS Magic and our other tools as people join, change roles or leave

  • Troubleshoot calling, callback and voicemail issues with agents, and work with Vonage support on open cases

  • Manage our business phone numbers: assignments, releases, and requesting spam-label removal with the carriers (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile)

  • 2+ years in IT help desk, technical support or contact center support

  • Strong troubleshooting skills: you can take a vague "it's not working," find the cause, and fix it or explain it clearly

  • A track record of working independently: self-motivated, organized and good at managing your own time

  • Excellent written and spoken English; most communication is written, in tickets and Slack

  • Reliable internet and a quiet workspace for the full 7:30 to 3:30 CT schedule

Nice to have

  • Salesforce Administrator certification

  • Vonage Contact Center (VCC) or another cloud contact center platform

  • SMS platforms, telecom or phone number management

  • Experience supporting sales teams

About the Company
Our client is a U.S.-based global distributor of plastic compounds and polymer materials, serving customers across multiple international markets.

We are looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Operations CSR & Shipping Document Coordinator to manage customer orders and international shipments from order entry through final delivery.
This role combines customer operations, international logistics, export documentation, and freight coordination. You'll manage orders, carrier bookings, vessel schedules, shipping documents, shipment tracking, and communication with customers and logistics partners.

What You'll Do

  • Monitor warehouse activity to prevent late ingates and container rolls.
  • Maintain order summaries and provide shipment visibility to commercial teams.
  • Track shipments and proactively resolve delays or operational issues.
Export Documentation & Customer Support
  • Prepare international shipping documentation, including Bills of Lading (BOL), Certificates of Analysis (COA), Commercial Invoices (CI), and Packing Lists (PL).
  • Prepare export declarations and Bills of Lading for ocean exports.

  • Ensure shipping documents are accurate, complete, and delivered on time.
  • Communicate shipping details and documentation requirements to customers.
  • Onboard new customers and maintain accurate information.
  • Manage delivery-related claims and coordinate resolution with internal and external stakeholders.
Qualifications
Required
  • 2–3 years of experience in international trade, logistics, shipping operations, supply chain, or a related field.
  • Experience with international shipping and export documentation.
  • Experience working with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and/or NVOCCs.
  • Understanding of BOLs, Commercial Invoices, Packing Lists, and related export documents.
  • Microsoft Excel proficiency.
  • Strong professional English communication skills.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Strong organization, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple shipments, priorities, and deadlines independently.
Preferred
  • Experience in the plastic resin, polymer, chemicals, or manufacturing industry.
  • Experience interpreting Letters of Credit.
  • Experience coordinating railcar and ocean shipments.
  • Experience establishing rates or services with third-party carriers.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, International Trade, or a related field.
What Success Looks Like
  • Orders and shipping documents are processed accurately and on time.
  • International shipments are proactively monitored from order through delivery.
  • Carrier bookings, vessel schedules, and deadlines are effectively managed.
  • Potential delays and documentation issues are identified and resolved quickly.
  • Customers and internal teams receive accurate and timely updates.
  • Multiple shipments are managed without sacrificing attention to detail.
Why Join Us?
  • $1,500–$2,500 USD/month compensation.
  • Fully remote opportunity from selected Latin American countries.
  • Exposure to international trade, ocean freight, rail transportation, and export operations.
  • Work directly with international customers and logistics partners.

Important Notes
This is an international logistics and operations role, not a traditional customer-service-only position. Candidates should have practical experience with shipping operations and export documentation.
Strong professional English, Excel proficiency, and excellent attention to detail are essential.

This is a remote/telecommute position.

Ziply Fiber is a local internet service provider dedicated to elevating the connected lives of the communities we serve. We offer the fastest home internet in the nation, a refreshingly great customer experience, and affordable plans that put customers in charge.

As our state-of-the-art fiber network expands, so does our need for team members who can help us grow and realize our goals.

Our Company Values:

  • Genuinely Caring:We treat customers and colleagues like neighbors, with empathy and full attention.
  • Empowering You:We help customers choose what is best for them, and we support employees in implementing new ideas and solutions.
  • Innovation and Improvement:We constantly seek ways to improve how we serve customers and each other.
  • Earning Your Trust:We build trust through clear, honest, human communication.

Job Summary

The Program Manager, Fiber Design & Construction (FDC) - Subsidy Builds is a hands-on program leader responsible for planning and delivering fiber construction programs supported by federal, state and local subsidy funding. This role leads schedule, budget, location-data, milestone, risk and compliance management and partners with engineering, design, permitting, construction, operations, vendors, Finance and Regulatory & External Affairs to move subsidized builds from award through customer-ready service activation and certification.

This Program Manager brings structure, clarity and accountability to a complex portfolio of subsidized builds. The ideal candidate translates funding requirements, location-level data and construction dependencies into clear plans and actions while maintaining a recurring operating rhythm that keeps teams aligned, risks visible and milestone certifications audit-ready.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Essential Duties and Responsibilities listed below are a range of duties performed by the employee and not intended to reflect all duties performed.

Strategic Alignment & Communication

·Translate subsidy award commitments and build strategy into integrated work plans, prioritized actions and measurable deliverables.

·Reinforce disciplined reporting through structured updates on completed work, upcoming milestones, compliance deliverables, risks and support needed.

·Develop and present executive reporting summarizing schedule performance, budget status, completed and remaining locations, compliance readiness, key risks and recovery actions.

·Maintain cross-functional alignment across engineering, design, permitting, construction, operations, vendors, Finance and Regulatory & External Affairs through recurring program reviews.

·Serve as the primary FDC program owner for assigned subsidy-funded portfolios and maintain accountability for buildout timelines, funded-location commitments, certification milestones and reporting deadlines.

·Establish recurring program, milestone, risk and compliance reviews and document decisions, owners, due dates and recovery plans.

Planning & Modeling

·Support sequencing and prioritization based on funding deadlines, construction readiness, resource availability, vendor capacity and permitting constraints.

·Validate planning inputs including eligible locations, award assumptions, design readiness, permitting status, construction scope and serviceability requirements.

·Build readiness and compliance checklists supporting transitions between design, permitting, construction, service activation and milestone certification.

·Analyze forecasts against subsidy buildout commitments, ready-for-sale objectives and funding milestones and identify recovery actions for schedule or location gaps.

·Surface high-cost, high-risk or potentially ineligible segments early and coordinate alternatives with engineering, design, Finance and Regulatory & External Affairs.

·Drive subsidy-funded programs from award and planning through construction completion, service activation and required certification.

·Monitor contractor and vendor performance and escalate issues affecting schedule, budget, funded-location commitments or compliance requirements.

Milestones & Dependencies

·Track program and location-level milestones across engineering, permitting, construction, service availability and required funding checkpoints.

·Maintain visibility into bottlenecks, aging tasks, location discrepancies, certification dependencies and cross-functional risks.

·Coordinate removal of blockers with engineering, permitting, construction, operations, vendors and Regulatory & External Affairs.

·Partner with FDC leadership to ensure subsidized projects achieve construction completion, service activation and funded-location targets within required timeframes.

Subsidy Program Governance, Compliance & GIS

·Maintain governance frameworks, documentation standards, escalation paths and workflows for subsidy-funded construction programs.

·Maintain working knowledge of applicable broadband subsidy programs, including BEAD, RDOF, ARPA/Capital Projects Fund and state or local grant-funded builds.

·Support milestone certifications and location-level reporting, including USAC HUBB submissions and other funding-administrator requirements, with Regulatory & External Affairs.

·Maintain accurate, audit-ready program documentation and workflows in SiteTracker and supporting systems, including as-builts, service availability, speed or latency evidence and certification records.

·Maintain and validate broadband serviceable-location data in Esri ArcGIS, IQGeo or comparable platforms and manage KMZ/KML transfers across GIS, engineering and reporting systems.

·Reconcile eligible and constructed locations against award records, the FCC National Broadband Map or BEAD fabric and support challenge, true-up and correction processes.

·Track spend against approved budgets, funding applications and capital forecasts; identify variances and coordinate mitigation plans with Finance, FDC leadership and Regulatory & External Affairs.

·Maintain milestone, WIP and risk scorecards and a live risk register for each assigned subsidy program.

·Monitor applicable FCC, NTIA, USAC and state broadband office guidance for changes affecting scope, schedule, reporting or documentation.

·Coordinate with state broadband offices, USAC and other funding administrators as directed by Regulatory & External Affairs.

·Coordinate internal readiness for audits, funding reviews and regulatory inquiries.

Other Duties

·Performs other duties as required to support the business and evolving organization.

Required Qualifications:

·High school diploma or GED.

·Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering, Telecommunications, Project Management, Business Administration or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

·Minimum of five (5) to seven (7) years of telecom program or project management experience, including fiber planning, engineering, permitting or construction.

·Strong end-to-end understanding of the fiber build lifecycle, network readiness and subsidized buildout obligations.

·Knowledge of permitting processes, third-party utility coordination and federal or state broadband subsidy requirements.

·Experience managing complex portfolios and converting location-level, construction and compliance work queues into structured execution plans.

·Proven success driving accountability in cross-functional teams.

·Demonstrated success leading large, cross-functional telecommunications construction programs involving engineering, permitting, construction, operations, finance, vendors and regulatory stakeholders.

·Strong analytical skills connecting schedule, budget, GIS, location and compliance data to broader program outcomes.

·Effective communicator able to simplify complex funding, regulatory and construction requirements and influence technical, operational and cross-functional teams.

·Highly organized with strong attention to detail and proven ability to manage competing priorities.

·Proficient with Microsoft Office, Smartsheet, program tracking tools and GIS or location-management platforms.

Preferred Qualifications:

·PMP or equivalent project management certification.

·Experience with SiteTracker, Esri ArcGIS, IQGeo, KMZ/KML, address-management systems, USAC HUBB reporting or comparable funding-reporting platforms.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

·Ability to work independently and apply sound judgment and reasoning skills to a variety of situations.

·Ability to multi-task and collaborate effectively with other personnel to meet deadlines.

·Strong verbal and written communication, attention to detail, and organizational skills.

·Ability to work within critical deadlines.

·Ability to adjust to rapidly changing priorities and schedules.

·Ability to provide excellent customer service.

Work Authorization

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the US for any employer. Sponsorship is not available for this position.

Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential and marginal functions may require maintaining physical condition necessary for bending, stooping, sitting, walking, or standing for prolonged periods of time; most of time is spent sitting in a comfortable position with frequent opportunity to move about. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

Work Environment

Work is performed in an office setting with exposure to computer screens and requires extensive use of a computer, keyboard, mouse, and multi-line telephone system. The work is primarily a modern office setting.

At all times, Ziply Fiber must be your primary employer. Unless otherwise prohibited by law, employees may not hold outside employment nor be self-employed without obtaining approval in writing from Ziply Fiber. In holding outside employment or self-employment, employees should ensure that participation does not conflict with responsibilities to Ziply Fiber or its business interests.

Diverse Workforce / EEO:

Ziply Fiber is an equal opportunity employer. Ziply Fiber will consider all qualified candidates regardless of race, color, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, sexual orientation, veteran status, and the presence of a non-job-related handicap or disability or any other legally protected status.

Ziply Fiber requires a pre-employment background check as conditions of employment. Ziply Fiber may require a pre-employment drug screening.

Ziply Fiber is a drug free workplace.

jobs.excerpt: kurzbeschreibungStell dir vor, du arbeitest in einem Umfeld, in dem deine Expertise wirklich zählt und du maßgeblich zur Transformation und Optimierung von Geschäftsprozessen beitragen kannst.
jobs.description:
kurzbeschreibung

Stell dir vor, du arbeitest in einem Umfeld, in dem deine Expertise wirklich zählt und du maßgeblich zur Transformation und Optimierung von Geschäftsprozessen beitragen kannst.

Als Senior SAP Consultant (m/w/d) bei uns bist du nicht nur technischer Berater – du wirst zum strategischen Partner unserer Kunden, der ihnen hilft, ihre Geschäftsprozesse effizienter und nachhaltiger zu gestalten. Hier ist jede Entscheidung, jede Anpassung ein Schritt in Richtung einer zukunftssicheren, innovativen Organisation. Wenn du also eine Herausforderung suchst, die nicht nur technisches Know-how, sondern auch unternehmerisches Denken erfordert, bist du bei uns genau richtig.

deine aufgaben

In deiner Rolle als Senior SAP Consultant wirst du aktiv an der Analyse und Optimierung der Geschäftsprozesse unserer Kunden beteiligt sein. Du verstehst die individuellen Anforderungen der Unternehmen und entwickelst auf dieser Basis maßgeschneiderte Lösungen. Deine Erfahrung ermöglicht es dir, Geschäftsprozessabläufe fachlich zu konzipieren und diese in internen und externen Projekten systemseitig erfolgreich umzusetzen.

Ein wesentlicher Fokus deiner Arbeit liegt auf der Einführung von SAP Waste and Recycling oder unseren SAP IS-U Lösungen in Kundenprojekten. Dabei betreust du nicht nur die technischen Aspekte, sondern berätst auch strategisch, um Prozesse optimal auf die Bedürfnisse der Kunden anzupassen. Du begleitest und gestaltest Prozessänderungen und Verbesserungen, immer mit dem Ziel, nachhaltige und effiziente Lösungen zu implementieren.

Darüber hinaus übernimmst du die Verantwortung für das Customizing von SAP-Lösungen, die genau auf die Anforderungen des jeweiligen Kunden abgestimmt sind. Du sorgst dafür, dass alles reibungslos funktioniert, indem du intensive Tests der entwickelten Lösungen durchführst, um deren Qualität sicherzustellen.

Auch nach der Implementierung bleibst du in engem Kontakt mit den Kunden: Du organisierst Kundenschulungen, um den reibungslosen Übergang zu neuen Prozessen zu garantieren, und kümmerst dich um die Nachbetreuung der implementierten Lösungen. So stellst du sicher, dass alle Systeme optimal laufen und jederzeit anpassbar bleiben.

Mit einer Reisebereitschaft von 30-40%, abhängig von der jeweiligen Projektphase, kannst du direkt vor Ort mit den Kunden zusammenarbeiten, ihre Anforderungen noch besser verstehen und deine Expertise einbringen.

Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und mindestens Englisch Kenntnisse auf B2 Niveau runden dein Profil ab und machen dich zur idealen Verstärkung für unser Team.

dein profil

Du bringst einen (Fach-)Hochschulabschluss in Wirtschaftsinformatik, BWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Umweltmanagement oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich mit. In Projekten arbeitest du eigenständig und strukturiert, auch unter Belastung behältst du den Überblick und kannst flexibel auf Herausforderungen reagieren.
Als erfahrener Consultant hast du bereits unter Beweis gestellt, dass du eigenständig in Projekten arbeiten kannst und bereit bist, die Rolle des Teilprojektleiters in größeren Beratungsprojekten zu übernehmen. Du bist routiniert im Umgang mit Kunden, kannst sie sicher führen und kommunizierst klar und überzeugend auf allen Ebenen.
Fundierte Kenntnisse im Projektmanagement sowie in der Geschäftsprozessanalyse sind für dich selbstverständlich, und du verfügst über ein gutes Zeitmanagement sowie die nötige Eigeninitiative, um Projekte erfolgreich voranzutreiben.
Zudem bringst du sehr gute SAP-Kenntnisse in den Modulen SAP IS-U, EDM, Gerätemanagement, PM, SD, MM, FI oder CO mit, und Grundkenntnisse in ABAP sind von Vorteil. jobs.excerpt: DeepHealth is seeking a Product Leader to shape the next generation of PACS and diagnostic viewing within its Diagnostic Suite.
jobs.description:
DeepHealth is seeking a Product Leader to shape the next generation of PACS and diagnostic viewing within its Diagnostic Suite. This leader will define how radiologists access, review, compare, and interpret imaging studies, while enabling healthcare organizations to manage imaging reliably across sites and care settings.

The role combines strategic product leadership with hands-on expertise in radiology workflows. You will own the PACS and Viewer product direction, translate clinical needs into differentiated capabilities, and guide execution from discovery through launch and adoption. Success will be measured by an exceptional reading experience, dependable imaging operations, customer adoption, and sustainable business growth.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Set product direction. Establish a compelling vision and prioritized roadmap for PACS and Viewer, balancing clinical value, market differentiation, platform modernization, and commercial objectives.

  • Own the radiologist experience. Lead product discovery with radiologists across specialties. Translate observations of real reading workflows into intuitive navigation, fewer interruptions, and efficient access to relevant images and clinical information.

  • Advance diagnostic viewing. Define capabilities for hanging protocols, multi-monitor layouts, series navigation, longitudinal comparison, prior relevance, measurements, annotations, and modality-specific reading tools. Shape integration with advanced visualization and subspecialty applications.

  • Lead PACS capabilities. Set priorities for image ingestion, routing, storage, retrieval, reconciliation, sharing, and lifecycle management. Address the operational needs of PACS administrators, imaging informatics teams, and enterprise customers.

  • Deliver a connected diagnostic workspace. Partner with worklist, reporting, and AI product leaders to maintain patient and study context across applications, reduce duplicate actions, and integrate findings and measurements into the reading workflow.

  • Guide cloud adoption and interoperability. Define customer requirements for cloud and hybrid deployments, legacy PACS coexistence, archive migration, and access to historical studies. Prioritize reliable connectivity with modalities, RIS, EHR, and third-party imaging systems.

  • Make performance a product priority. Establish measurable expectations for time to first image, series navigation, prior availability, large-study responsiveness, and service reliability across representative customer environments.

  • Turn strategy into delivery. Maintain clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and release priorities. Resolve scope trade-offs with engineering and design, and coordinate clinical validation, pilot feedback, launch readiness, and post-release improvements.

  • Build the business. Develop investment proposals and contribute to pricing, packaging, competitive positioning, and sales enablement. Evaluate opportunities using customer value, revenue potential, delivery effort, and cost to serve.

  • Lead across teams. Align internal teams and technology partners around product outcomes. Mentor product managers and product owners, strengthen discovery practices, and communicate decisions clearly to customers and executives.

  • Measure impact. Track adoption, user satisfaction, workflow efficiency, support burden, retention, and product economics. Use evidence to refine priorities and address gaps.

PLEASE NOTE: This is not an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and requirements of the position described above. Other functions may be assigned and management retains the right to add or change duties at any time.

Requirements

  • Minimum Qualifications, Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, health informatics, business, or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

  • At least 10 years of relevant healthcare technology experience, including 7 years in product management and significant responsibility for PACS or diagnostic viewer products.

  • Demonstrated success bringing commercial imaging software to market and improving products used in daily clinical practice.

  • Deep understanding of radiologist reading workflows, multi-modality imaging, prior comparison, and enterprise PACS operations.

  • Ability to evaluate diagnostic viewer usability and performance with clinicians and translate findings into actionable product decisions.

  • Practical knowledge of imaging interoperability, including DICOM, DICOMweb, HL7, FHIR, and relevant IHE workflows.

  • Experience with cloud or hybrid imaging products, enterprise integrations, and complex customer deployments.

  • Strong commercial judgment and the ability to make disciplined investment and prioritization decisions.

  • Experience leading distributed, cross-functional teams and influencing senior stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience modernizing an established PACS or migrating customers to a cloud-based imaging platform.

  • Familiarity with advanced visualization, mammography and tomosynthesis, or other demanding subspecialty workflows.

  • Experience integrating AI results, structured imaging data, and reporting tools into diagnostic applications.

  • Experience managing or mentoring product teams.

  • Familiarity with medical-device product development, clinical validation, usability engineering, and quality management processes.

Quality Standards

  • Incorporate patient safety, diagnostic integrity, privacy, and security into product decisions.

  • Partner with Quality and Regulatory teams on intended use, risk controls, requirements traceability, and release evidence.

  • Maintain clear documentation and communicate product limitations, dependencies, and risks promptly.

  • Demonstrate accountability, respectful collaboration, and adherence to company policies.

  • Communicates, cooperates, and consistently functions professionally and harmoniously with all levels of supervision, co-workers, visitors, and vendors.

  • Demonstrates initiative, personal awareness, professionalism and integrity, and exercises confidentiality in all areas of performance.

  • Follows all local, regional and country laws concerning employment.

  • Follows all DeepHealth policies and procedures.

  • Follows data privacy, compliance, safety and confidentiality standards at all times.

  • Practices universal safety precautions.

  • Promotes good public relations on the phone and in person.

  • Adapts and is willing to learn new tasks, methods, and systems.

  • Reports to work regularly as scheduled; consistently punctual with respect to working hours, meal and rest breaks, and maintains satisfactory personal attendance in accordance with DeepHealth guidelines.

  • Completes job responsibilities in a quality and timely manner.

Travel

Travel for clinical observation, customer engagements, implementation reviews, and industry events as required; expected frequency will be confirmed for the position.

Working Environment

United States / Canada. Collaborate with geographically distributed teams and customers

Pluralsight is hiring a Director of Growth and Digital Marketing to run the digital engine supporting new-logo acquisition and customer expansion. We are looking for a hands-on builder who can establish the playbook, then scale it across the team to support long-term growth. You'll build campaigns that pull early engagement through to pipeline and closed-won revenue, connecting awareness, nurture, and conversion across channels so interest turns into opportunities. You will also lead the evolution of the team and operating model- creating clear ownership, stronger accountability, and the capabilities needed to scale. This role reports to the VP, Revenue Marketing.


Responsibilities:

  • Digital execution for partner teams
    • Translate briefs from cross-functional stakeholders into demand gen plans, traffic strategy, and budget recommendations to reach their pipeline goals.
    • Manage paid, email, and digital execution for global campaigns, reporting results back to campaign owners.
    • Build repeatable playbooks, templates, and intake processes so partner teams launch faster with consistent quality.

  • Owned growth programs
    • Develop and execute integrated multi-channel strategies that build awareness, generate demand, and pull prospects through to closed-won ARR.
    • Own always-on digital acquisition programs, including paid search, paid social, and lifecycle nurture, with accountability for pipeline contribution.
    • Own lifecycle programs across acquisition, nurture, customer engagement, retention, and expansion, using behavioral signals and segmentation to move customers and prospects to the next best action.
    • Allocate the digital budget across channels and programs based on pipeline and bookings, and move spend when the data says to.
    • Hands-on optimization of new programs, channels, and creative.
    • Direct the media agency as its strategic owner. Set priorities, manage scope, and run quarterly business reviews.
    • Build scalable digital and ABM playbooks that can be deployed across segments, regions, strategic accounts, and solution campaigns.
  • Measurement, budget, and team
    • Track full-funnel performance from first engagement to closed-won ARR, sharing insights with campaign owners and marketing leadership.
    • Perform post-mortems on closed-won and closed-lost pipeline to reallocate spend and sharpen playbooks.
    • Manage financial forecasting, pacing, and reconciliation with Finance.

  • Demonstrated ability to measure digital pipeline contribution in the CRM beyond platform reporting, using multi-touch attribution or incrementality testing.

  • Experience supporting ABM and strategic-account motions in partnership with Sales and Revenue Marketing.

Criar, ajustar e manter políticas, regras, assinaturas, listas de exceção e perfis de proteção, equilibrando segurança e disponibilidade dos serviços.
Conduzir processos de tuning e redução de falsos positivos, com acompanhamento de impacto junto às áreas de negócio, produto e desenvolvimento.
Realizar a análise de eventos e bloqueios em camada 7, identificando padrões de ataque, exploração de vulnerabilidades, abuso de APIs, scraping e atividade de bots.
Apoiar a definição de controles de proteção contra ataques volumétricos e de aplicação (DDoS L7, OWASP Top 10, credential stuffing, enumeração, abuso de funcionalidades).
Participar do onboarding de novas aplicações, domínios e APIs nas soluções de proteção, garantindo cobertura adequada dos ativos expostos.
Acompanhar indicadores de eficácia dos controles, cobertura de proteção, volumetria de bloqueios e maturidade das políticas aplicadas.
Participar do processo de Gestão de certificados digitais da organização (mTLS, TLS, eCPF, eCPNJ).
Apoiar a administração, o monitoramento e a sustentação dos Hardware Security Modules (HSM), garantindo a guarda segura, o ciclo de vida e o uso controlado das chaves criptográficas corporativas, incluindo geração, rotação, backup, custódia, revogação e descarte, bem como a integração dos HSMs com as aplicações, APIs e serviços que dependem de assinatura digital e criptografia, assegurando disponibilidade, segregação de funções, trilhas de auditoria e conformidade com as políticas internas e requisitos regulatórios aplicáveis.

Operações de segurança (SecOps)

Atuar na sustentação, administração e otimização das ferramentas de segurança do ambiente, garantindo funcionamento, atualização e aderência às boas práticas.
Apoiar as atividades de monitoramento, triagem, investigação e resposta a incidentes de segurança, especialmente os relacionados a aplicações e serviços expostos.
Contribuir com a engenharia de detecção, propondo casos de uso, regras e melhorias de visibilidade a partir dos eventos gerados pelos controles de proteção.
Apoiar ações de hardening, redução de superfície de ataque, correção de vulnerabilidades e fortalecimento de configurações.
Participar de análises técnicas de incidentes, causas-raiz, contenção, erradicação e lições aprendidas, incluindo atuação em salas de crise quando acionado.
Interagir com as áreas de Infraestrutura, Redes, Cloud, Arquitetura, AppSec, DevSecOps, CSIRT e fornecedores na condução de demandas técnicas.

Processos, documentação e governança técnica

Elaborar e manter documentação técnica, procedimentos operacionais, runbooks e padrões de configuração das soluções sob sua responsabilidade.
Apoiar auditorias internas, externas, demandas regulatórias e curadorias de evidências relacionadas aos controles de proteção de aplicações.
Atuar como referência técnica para analistas juniores e plenos, realizando mentoria, revisão técnica e disseminação de conhecimento.
Apoiar a avaliação técnica de novas soluções, provas de conceito e roadmap de evolução das defesas da coordenação.
Contribuir para a melhoria contínua dos processos operacionais, automação de rotinas e padronização das entregas da área.Experiência consolidada em operações de segurança da informação em ambientes corporativos de médio/grande porte;
Vivência prática na administração de soluções de WAF e proteção de aplicações e APIs (configuração, tuning, políticas, análise de eventos);
Conhecimento de OWASP Top 10, OWASP API Security, técnicas de ataque a aplicações web e respectivos controles de mitigação;
Conhecimento de protocolos e tecnologias web: HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, DNS, proxies reversos, balanceadores, CDN e arquiteturas de publicação de serviços;
Familiaridade com controles de segurança de infraestrutura: firewall, IPS/IDS, EDR, SIEM, gestão de vulnerabilidades e segmentação de rede;
Noções de ambientes cloud, containers, microsserviços, APIs e integração com pipelines de desenvolvimento;
Capacidade de análise de logs, correlação de eventos e investigação técnica de incidentes.

Desejável

Conhecimento em automação e scripting para apoio às rotinas operacionais;
Certificações de mercado em segurança ofensiva, defensiva, cloud ou nas soluções de proteção de aplicações utilizadas.

jobs.description:
★ PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH ★

Operations CSR & Shipping Document Coordinator

Location: Remote – Brazil, Colombia, Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, or Ecuador
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote
Employment Type: Full-Time Contractor | Potential Full-Time Employee Transition After 6 Months
Industry: Manufacturing & Supply Chain / International Trade & Logistics
Compensation:$1,500–$2,500 USD/month
Experience:2–3 Years
English Proficiency:Strong Professional English Required


About the Company
Our client is a U.S.-based global distributor of plastic compounds and polymer materials, serving customers across multiple international markets.
The company operates in a fast-paced supply chain environment requiring close coordination between customers, warehouses, carriers, freight forwarders, and commercial teams to ensure international shipments are executed accurately and on time.
About the Role
We are looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented Operations CSR & Shipping Document Coordinator to manage customer orders and international shipments from order entry through final delivery.
This role combines customer operations, international logistics, export documentation, and freight coordination. You'll manage orders, carrier bookings, vessel schedules, shipping documents, shipment tracking, and communication with customers and logistics partners.
The ideal candidate has 2–3 years of relevant experience, strong professional English, and exceptional attention to detail when managing multiple shipments, documents, and deadlines.
What You'll Do
Order & Shipping Operations

  • Manage customer orders from receipt through delivery.
  • Create and maintain Sales Orders and Sales Contracts.
  • Coordinate pickups and deliveries with customers, carriers, warehouses, and internal teams.
  • Manage carrier bookings, cut-offs, and vessel schedules with freight forwarders and ocean carriers/NVOCCs.
  • Track vessel shipments and railcar movements, including the return of empty railcars.
  • Monitor warehouse activity to prevent late ingates and container rolls.
  • Maintain order summaries and provide shipment visibility to commercial teams.
  • Track shipments and proactively resolve delays or operational issues.
Export Documentation & Customer Support
  • Prepare international shipping documentation, including Bills of Lading (BOL), Certificates of Analysis (COA), Commercial Invoices (CI), and Packing Lists (PL).
  • Prepare export declarations and Bills of Lading for ocean exports.
  • Review and interpret Letters of Credit when required.
  • Ensure shipping documents are accurate, complete, and delivered on time.
  • Communicate shipping details and documentation requirements to customers.
  • Onboard new customers and maintain accurate information.
  • Manage delivery-related claims and coordinate resolution with internal and external stakeholders.
Qualifications
Required
  • 2–3 years of experience in international trade, logistics, shipping operations, supply chain, or a related field.
  • Experience with international shipping and export documentation.
  • Experience working with ocean carriers, freight forwarders, and/or NVOCCs.
  • Understanding of BOLs, Commercial Invoices, Packing Lists, and related export documents.
  • Microsoft Excel proficiency.
  • Strong professional English communication skills.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
  • Strong organization, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple shipments, priorities, and deadlines independently.
Preferred
  • Experience in the plastic resin, polymer, chemicals, or manufacturing industry.
  • Experience interpreting Letters of Credit.
  • Experience coordinating railcar and ocean shipments.
  • Experience establishing rates or services with third-party carriers.
  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, International Trade, or a related field.
What Success Looks Like
  • Orders and shipping documents are processed accurately and on time.
  • International shipments are proactively monitored from order through delivery.
  • Carrier bookings, vessel schedules, and deadlines are effectively managed.
  • Potential delays and documentation issues are identified and resolved quickly.
  • Customers and internal teams receive accurate and timely updates.
  • Multiple shipments are managed without sacrificing attention to detail.
Why Join Us?
  • $1,500–$2,500 USD/month compensation.
  • Fully remote opportunity from selected Latin American countries.
  • Exposure to international trade, ocean freight, rail transportation, and export operations.
  • Work directly with international customers and logistics partners.
  • U.S. holidays during the initial contractor period.
  • Potential opportunity to transition to a full-time employee position after approximately six months, subject to performance and company requirements.

Important Notes
This is an international logistics and operations role, not a traditional customer-service-only position. Candidates should have practical experience with shipping operations and export documentation.
Strong professional English, Excel proficiency, and excellent attention to detail are essential.

This is a remote/telecommute position.

Marin General Hospital dba MarinHealth Medical Center

$36.77 - $55.15

8 Hour (days) (United States of America)

40

Job Description Summary:

Ready to make a measurable impact across a growing healthcare network? MarinHealth is seeking a knowledgeable and proactive 340B Coordinator to oversee the administration, compliance, and strategic optimization of the 340B Drug Pricing Program across MarinHealth Medical Center and nine affiliated sites. Partnering with pharmacy leadership and cross-functional teams, this role helps ensure program excellence while supporting patient access initiatives and financial stewardship. Eligible candidates may work remotely from anywhere within California.

Job Requirements, Prerequisites and Essential Functions:

Job Specifications:

Education:

  • Two (2) year degree (or expected completion within one (1) year) or better and five (5) years of experience in hospital pharmacy experience.

  • Two years of experience in a 340B program preferred.

Experience:

  • Working knowledge of 340B Drug Program and contract pharmacy operations. Familiar with 340B split billing software and configurations.

  • Two years of pharmacy purchasing and inventory management experience or related experience.

License and Certifications:

  • Registered Pharmacy Technician (PHRMTECH-R) required at hire.

  • Integrative Agitation Management (IAMTAC) Required within 30 days of hire.

  • National Pharmacy Technician (PHARM-C) Certification preferred at hire.

Prerequisite Skills:

  • Ability to use Microsoft office products including Excel, Word, and Outlook. Critical thinking skills are imperative for the analysis of 340B program.

  • Ability to analyze, understands, and uses statistical and financial report data to identify issues, trends, or exceptions to drive improvement of results and find solutions. Leadership skills are required to effectively implement changes throughout the organization to improve the 340B program.

  • Must have good organization skills, work independently and prioritize multiple projects and objectives in a rapidly changing environment.

  • Employees in this position must be able to demonstrate the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care and/or service based on the physical, psycho/social, educational, safety, and related criteria appropriate to the age of the patients served in his/her assigned service area.

Patient Privacy (HIPAA Compliance):

  • Employees in this position have access to protected health information. The protected health information a person in this position can access includes demographics, date of service, insurance/billing, medical record summary information, and all other information that may be contained in patient records. This position requires patient health information to perform the functions outlined as part of this position description.

Duties And Responsibilities:

Essential

  • Responds to all requests regarding 340B activities.

  • Collaborates with 340B contract pharmacy vendors and pharmacy wholesalers to support the contract pharmacy network.

  • Serves as the liaison for 340B software vendors and wholesale distributors to manage and oversee compliance with contractual terms and conditions.

  • Supports installation and continuous utilization of vendor software.

  • Provides problem resolution and appropriate follow-up with the vendor and wholesalers when necessary.

  • Maintain a collaborative relationship with contract pharmacies and provides timely resolution and/or communication of any issues, when these relationships are established.

  • Serve as the primary link between wholesale distributors, contract pharmacies, manufacturers, legal counsel, prime vendor program, supply chain, 340B Health, split-billing software vendor, HRSA/OPA, pharmacy leadership and others as relates to the operation and management of contract and 340B program business.

  • Coordinates 340B needs with the buyer and Pharmacy IT.

  • Pharmacy staffing when required.

FINANCE

  • Plans and organizes the development and implementation of the 340B program and the contract pharmacy network:

    • Takes a lead role in the development, planning and integration efforts related to the 340B program,

    • Evaluates pharmacies for inclusion into the contract pharmacy network,

    • Establishes marketing of the program to contract pharmacies of interest,

    • Establishes a contractual relationship with the pharmacies,

    • Maximizes operational efficiency of the contract pharmacy network,

    • Performs periodic site visits at contract pharmacies when appropriate and

    • Reviews and provides recommendations to pharmacy leadership on pharmacy contracting and other 340B opportunities and strategies while assessing the impact from a financial, clinical and operational perspective.

  • Maintains the mapping of the split-billing software, works to ensure 340B drug purchases maximize pharmaceutical cost savings and works in conjunction with Revenue Integrity to investigate, correct, and modify any billing NDC discrepancies and pricing issues.

  • Review 340B Contract Pharmacy pharmaceutical invoices prior to final approval by Director of Pharmacy; compile and prepare invoices for the amount due for Retail Pharmacy.

  • Computes monthly 340B savings report from drug wholesaler; reviews amount due from Retail Pharmacy and follows up on discrepancies or past due amounts.

  • Assists Pharmacy Buyer and Pharmacist, as needed, for GPO/WAC/340B purchase determination and preparing invoices and purchasing/financial reports.

QUALITY/SAFETY/COMPLIANCE/ETHICS

  • Reviews policies and procedures to ensure effectiveness and compliance with state and federal regulations related to 340B program management and contract pharmacy operations.

  • Designs an efficient process to reconcile any issues with drug ordering, delivery and payment.

  • Remains informed of changes in policies or procedures, 340B related legislation, articles, white papers, and document briefs that could affect the program structure.

  • Assures appropriate safeguards and 340B integrity.

  • Develops and monitors standard operating procedures for the 340B program in its entirety and contract pharmacies.

  • Works with contract pharmacies to develop standard operating procedures for 340B multiple contract pharmacy processes.

  • Provides periodic reports to the Director of Compliance and Ethics regarding adherence to 340B, audit results (internal and external), effectiveness and regulatory updates.

SERVICE

  • Reports savings of the program [monthly, weekly, biweekly, etc.].

  • Assesses opportunities for cost savings and business improvement in 340B contract pharmacy utilization and prepares statements for this purpose.

  • Collaborates with departments, sites and staff representatives to communicate improvements and promote broad participation in 340B activities across the organization.

  • Leads and facilitates priority 340B projects to the final outcome.

  • Provides ongoing training, education, and communication required for 340B program

  • Assist Pharmacy Director and CFO with HRSA and manufacturer audits.

GROWTH/INNOVATION

  • Collaborates with information technology (IT) and decision support resources in assisting sites, departments, service lines and individuals in the identification of information or data needs to support 340B activities.

  • Performs quality assurance audits on all aspects of the organization’s 340B program on a continuous basis including contract pharmacy operations, financial transactions, and patient and provider qualifications:

    • Evaluates the oversight of the program,

    • Evaluates OPA database accuracy for eligible sites,

    • Reviews 340B purchase history to ensure that drugs being purchased on 340B accounts are drugs being utilized accurately for outpatient use and

    • Evaluates 340B inventory replenishment for each pharmacy to confirm that accumulation, reduction and reconciliation are occurring as expected.

  • Prepares audit findings, reports, graphs, and charts of data analysis and delivers presentations to work group committee on a regular basis.

  • Prepares conclusions, predictions, and develops recommendations based on research to track and manage essential aspects of the program and make improvements and/or ensure compliance.

  • Monitors changes that have been made per recommendations to evaluate success and suggests further improvements based on results.

Secondary (not modifiable)

Ability to work effectively with a variety of personnel with backgrounds varied in education and skill sets. Must be able function as a team leader. Must have good negotiation skills and be able to interact with internal staff, system vendors and outside consultants in a professional, effective method.

Global ChangeFacilitator - Supply Resilience

Help strengthen the global biopharmaceutical supply chain and make a lasting impact on the delivery of medicines to patients.

Make a difference to the future of medicine

What if your ability to bring people together could help solve some of the biggest challenges facing the global pharmaceutical supply chain?

At BioPhorum, we bring together experts from across the global biopharmaceutical industry to collaborate on shared challenges, exchange knowledge and turn collective expertise into meaningful change. Established in 2004, we are a business-to-business membership organisation working with more than 150 organisations, including 18 of the 20 largest global biopharmaceutical companies. Through our collaborative network, more than 7,000 subject matter experts contribute to over 90 initiatives designed to improve the industry.

We are looking for a Global Change Facilitator to join our Supply Resilience Phorum, helping biopharmaceutical manufacturers, suppliers and logistics providers work together to build a more resilient, agile and sustainable global supply chain.

This is an opportunity to combine your scientific understanding, project management expertise and stakeholder engagement skills to address complex industry challenges and support the reliable delivery of high-quality medicines to patients worldwide.

Be at the heart of global supply resilience

About BioPhorum Supply Resilience

BioPhorum Supply Resilience brings together 34 member organisations, including many of the world's leading pharmaceutical companies, to strengthen the inbound biopharmaceutical supply chain. By sharing knowledge, experience and best practice, our members work collectively to anticipate risks, improve supply chain performance and drive innovation across the industry.

Global events, geopolitical uncertainty, increasing demand for raw materials and consumables, and evolving regulatory requirements continue to place pressure on pharmaceutical supply networks. Our members collaborate to develop practical solutions that improve supply chain visibility, strengthen risk management, enhance demand forecasting and support business continuity.

Through dedicated workstreams, members explore opportunities to advance digital transformation, improve traceability, promote regional manufacturing capabilities, address emerging materials of concern and encourage regulatory alignment. The Phorum also develops industry guidance, practical tools and strategic frameworks that help organisations assess their capabilities and identify opportunities for improvement.

By bringing together expertise from across the supply chain, BioPhorum Supply Resilience helps turn shared challenges into coordinated industry action, supporting a safer, more adaptable and sustainable supply network that ultimately benefits patients.

As Global Change Facilitator, you will play a central role in this collaboration. You will guide industry experts through complex discussions, help translate challenges into structured projects and ensure that collective knowledge delivers meaningful, measurable outcomes.

What will you be doing?

  • Lead and facilitate workstreams: Guide a portfolio of collaborative initiatives, helping members define priorities, agree objectives and deliver outcomes aligned with BioPhorum's strategy and governance.
  • Bring industry experts together: Create engaging, inclusive meetings that encourage open discussion, draw out specialist knowledge and build strong working relationships across manufacturers, suppliers and logistics providers.

jobs.description:
About Us

Integrity360 is a leading independent cybersecurity and PCI specialist operating across Europe, Africa, the Caribbean, and North America. The company has office locations in Ireland, the UK, Bulgaria, Italy, Sweden, Spain, Lithuania, Ukraine, Africa, the Caribbean, and Canada, supported by seven Security Operations Centres (SOCs) located in Dublin, Sofia, Madrid, Stockholm, Rome, Johannesburg and Cape Town.

With over 780 employees, including more than 585 dedicated cybersecurity professionals, Integrity360 delivers a full suite of professional, support, and managed security services. These span the complete cyber risk lifecycle, from identification and prevention to detection, response, and recovery. Integrity360 supports over 3000 mid-market and enterprise organisations across sectors including financial services, insurance, government, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, and utilities.

At Integrity360, people come first. We invest heavily in learning, development and progression, fostering a dynamic culture where innovation, collaboration and continuous growth are at the heart of what we do. If you're ready to take your cyber security career to the next level, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Role / Responsibilities

As a Microsoft Security Engineer, you will be responsible for onboarding clients to our managed security service, with Microsoft Sentinel at the centre of the solution. You will configure and integrate Sentinel environments, onboard and validate log sources, and prepare each deployment for effective monitoring and operational handover to the Security Operations Centre.

Your primary focus will be the technical delivery of new Microsoft Sentinel onboardings. This includes workspace and connector configuration, data collection design, log-source integration, ingestion filtering, validation, detection tuning and the production of high-level design and implementation documentation. You will work closely with clients, architects and SOC teams to ensure each deployment is supportable, secure and aligned with the contracted service scope.

The role also requires hands-on experience, or a clear ability to develop quickly, in onboarding Microsoft Defender XDR workloads such as Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Cloud Apps. You will help establish the integrations, policies and operational workflows required to provide joined-up detection and response across the Microsoft security ecosystem.

This is a client-facing engineering role within Professional Services, reporting to the Head of Cloud Security & Microsoft Security Services. You will manage assigned onboarding activities from discovery and design through implementation, testing, documentation and handover. You will be supported by an experienced team and have access to training and certification opportunities across Microsoft security technologies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver end-to-end onboarding of client Microsoft Sentinel environments into the MSSP service.
  • Configure Sentinel workspaces, content solutions, data connectors, analytics rules, automation rules, watchlists, workbooks and related components in accordance with approved designs and service standards.
  • Run technical discovery sessions to identify log sources, connectivity requirements, data volumes, retention needs, dependencies and onboarding priorities.
  • Onboard Microsoft, third-party, cloud, network, identity and application log sources using supported collection methods, including Azure Monitor Agent, Data Collection Rules, APIs, syslog, CEF and custom connectors where appropriate.
  • Design and implement data filtering and transformation to improve signal quality, control ingestion costs and ensure the service receives the telemetry required for monitoring and detection.
  • Validate data ingestion, parsing, field mapping, timestamps, health and coverage, and troubleshoot issues across source systems, collectors, networks and Azure services.
  • Tune analytics rules, alert logic and incident generation in collaboration with SOC and detection engineering teams to reduce unnecessary noise while maintaining appropriate coverage.
  • Onboard and integrate Microsoft Defender XDR workloads, including Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Identity, Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Cloud Apps.
  • Produce accurate high-level designs, implementation plans, configuration records, test evidence, operational runbooks and handover documentation.
  • Coordinate with clients, project managers, architects, SOC analysts and service teams to manage dependencies, risks, actions and readiness for service transition.
  • Apply repeatable engineering standards, peer review and change control, and contribute improvements to onboarding templates, technical patterns and internal procedures.
  • Support troubleshooting and remediation during onboarding and early-life support, escalating product or service dependencies where required.
  • Undertake occasional travel where required to support client delivery.

Essential

  • Hands-on experience deploying, configuring or supporting Microsoft Sentinel in production or customer environments.
  • Practical knowledge of Sentinel data connectors, Log Analytics workspaces, Azure Monitor Agent, Data Collection Rules, syslog and CEF collection patterns.
  • Strong Kusto Query Language skills for data validation, troubleshooting, investigation and detection tuning.
  • Experience onboarding and troubleshooting log sources across Microsoft 365, Azure, endpoints, identity, network, security and third-party platforms.
  • Understanding of ingestion filtering, data transformation, parsing, normalisation, retention and the cost implications of security telemetry.
  • Experience creating clear technical designs and delivery documentation, including HLDs, implementation plans, test records and operational handover materials.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Defender XDR and the integration of its workloads with Microsoft Sentinel.
  • Sound understanding of SIEM operations, detection engineering principles, incident workflows and the requirements of a managed security service.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across Azure, APIs, identity, networking and data collection components.
  • Confident written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work directly with technical and non-technical client stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage assigned work independently while collaborating effectively with project, architecture, SOC and service teams.

Desired

  • Experience working for an MSSP, MDR provider, Security Operations Centre or security-focused professional services team.
  • Development of custom log parsers, KQL functions, ASIM-compatible content or other normalisation patterns for non-standard data sources.
  • Experience with DevOps pipelines and source control for Microsoft Sentinel content, configuration and deployment.
  • Practical knowledge of detection as code, including versioning, testing, peer review and controlled promotion of analytics content between environments.
  • Experience with infrastructure as code and automation using technologies such as Bicep, ARM templates, Terraform, PowerShell, Azure CLI, Logic Apps or APIs.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Sentinel repositories, content management and repeatable multi-customer deployment patterns.
  • Experience integrating Microsoft security services across tenants, subscriptions or delegated administration models such as Azure Lighthouse.
  • Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK and its application to detection coverage and use-case mapping.

Desired Qualifications

  • Microsoft Certified: Security Operations Analyst Associate (SC-200).

jobs.excerpt: Who We AreGreat Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

What We Build

Our products—Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom, Geodes, and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

  • Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.

  • Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

Where We’re Headed

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.


Job Purpose

The Senior Data Analyst, Enterprise Analytics is responsible for leading the delivery of actionable insights that drive data-driven strategy and performance across the organization. This role owns the design and execution of complex, high-impact analytics initiatives, develops advanced analyses, and architects reusable assets to empower decision-making and operational excellence at scale. The Senior Data Analyst serves as a subject matter expert and thought partner to senior business stakeholders, ensuring analytics solutions are strategically aligned and forward-looking. This role also provides technical mentorship and guidance to analysts and non-expert users across the organization.


Responsibilities

The duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Partner with senior leadership to frame ambiguous business problems, shape the analytical approach, and deliver solutions that hold up under real decision-making pressure — including knowing when the right call is not to build something.

  • Resolve conflicting metric definitions across departments and help establish shared business semantics that leadership can trust.

  • Design and own semantic models and reporting frameworks that serve multiple departments at once, balancing performance, reusability, and governance rather than optimizing for a single team's request.

  • Pull together information from systems that were never designed to talk to each other — CRM, ERP, marketing platforms, ad hoc files — and turn it into something durable rather than a one-off answer.

  • Architect and maintain enterprise-level dashboards where long-term accuracy and maintainability matter as much as the initial insight.

  • Document the reasoning behind analyses and metric logic well enough that someone else could pick up the work a year later.

  • Set standards for how analytics work gets built and reused, raising the bar across the organization rather than just within this role.

  • Mentor analysts and enable self-service users to build sound data products on their own.

Requirements

Requirements

  • 4+ years of experience in analytics, analytics engineering, or data-focused roles, with real accountability for analytics deliverables from framing through delivery — not just executing tickets.

  • Advanced, hands-on fluency with a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, or similar), including complex query work and performance tuning, running on a cloud platform — Azure preferred, AWS also relevant.

  • Comfort using code, not just point-and-click tools, to manipulate, analyze, and visualize data (Python).

  • Real experience designing and maintaining a semantic model or metric layer that had to serve more than one audience with different — sometimes conflicting — needs, including dimensional modeling concepts like star schemas and slowly changing dimensions.

  • Experience bringing basic software engineering discipline (version control, code review, modular and documented work) to analytics, which is too often treated casually.

  • Experience reconciling messy, overlapping systems of record such as CRM, ERP, and marketing platforms.

  • Experience building validation checks after having been burned by a silent data quality failure before.

  • A track record of turning a vague ask from a senior stakeholder into a scoped project, and communicating results in terms that land with that audience.

  • Experience mentoring others or setting standards that outlasted your own involvement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Interest in K-12 public education and how data moves from a district leader's dashboard down to a classroom-level decision.

  • Exposure to AWS as a secondary cloud environment alongside Azure.

  • Familiarity with advanced analytics techniques such as forecasting, segmentation, or scenario modeling.

  • Familiarity with data modeling and pipeline concepts (star/snowflake schema, entity-relationship modeling, ETL/ELT).

  • Experience helping stand up or mature an analytics function, rather than only working within an established one.

Required Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Business, or a related quantitative discipline.

Status

Full-time

Location

Remote

The expected base salary range for this position is $90,000-$100,000, however the offered salarymay be higher or lower than the above range dependent on numerous factors including, but not limited to location, work experience, skills and internal equity considerations.
